title: Ways to Split Array Into Three Subarrays
summary: Determine the count of valid ways to divide an array into three contiguous subarrays such that the sum of the left subarray is less than or equal to the mid subarray, and the mid subarray is less than or equal to the right subarray.
statement: Determine the count of valid ways to divide an array into three contiguous subarrays such that the sum of the left subarray is less than or equal to the mid subarray, and the mid subarray is less than or equal to the right subarray. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Split it into three nonempty contiguous parts and count splits with left sum <= middle sum <= right sum, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Nonnegative values make prefix sums sorted, so valid middle endpoints form one interval.
For every left endpoint, binary-search the first middle sum at least left and the last at most right.
Search prefix >= 2*left and prefix <= floor((total+left)/2), excluding the final index.
These two bounds are algebraically equivalent to left<=middle and middle<=right; every boundary pair is counted once.

tests.explanation: The three valid boundary pairs produce the required count three.
